title: The Bobby Trivia Dating Show
summary: Chapter 26 opens with a Mangchi song that moves from school-shooting and suicide imagery toward survival, then becomes an unusually useful failure report on DVDASA's attempt at a produced segment. Bobby Trivia revives Saelee Oh's year-old matchmaking premise while drinking, arranges three private dates, confirms the studio appearance only a day before recording, tells the only available date not to turn back because a one-person confrontation might be awkward, and begins the episode without any of the dates present. The cast directly calls this bad production and acknowledges that absent people should be able to answer. Saelee's current position supersedes the old premise: she does not want a boyfriend, wants to attend events normally, and objects to being reduced to weed and dating rather than her art. The archive therefore retains the off-air date chronology without names, wealth, family, ancestry, residence or private phone details, and treats every future appearance as a new invitation. Her November 2 testimony adds a needed women's-safety perspective: asymmetric fan knowledge felt creepy, one attendee's conduct was enough to change the event, another woman was reportedly groped after being announced single, and a room of strangers knew intimate details. The cake/suit conflict separates video evidence, intent, impact, labor and remedy. Video confirms Saelee threw cake at Critter; she says she meant play, did not know the suit's significance, apologizes and offers to pay, while Critter explains humiliation, cleanup and custom-clothing harm. Neither an audience poll nor the venue's disputed invoice determines the moral record. The subsequent young-roadie argument exposes David's punitive teaching philosophy: public humiliation is defended as efficient correction, while others demand private feedback, direct testimony and medical humility. The worker remains anonymous and no conclusion about his inner response is invented. A three-month-delayed Kevin Smith conflict shows why release lag matters: a perceived Comic-Con snub is discussed publicly, heard months later, disputed and finally resolved by phone. Digital-consent failures recur when friends use Saelee's phone and James Jean's accounts, impersonate them, send a deceptive explicit scrotum image and observe the recipient. The archive never displays the image or reproduces the private sext dossier. Date two is reported to begin with sexual questions, drinking pressure, mistaken identity and repeated hope that Saelee was a sex worker. Dinner payment does not erase those claims, and the absent date remains unidentified. Saelee's final oral-sex/nosebleed account distinguishes initial willingness from later wanting the prolonged act to end, no consent to intercourse, cocaine/sinus health context, blood exposure and a behavior-change conclusion. Humor is her coping frame, not proof the event was harmless. The episode also contains high-value product evidence: long intros frustrate listeners, lack of production prevents follow-through, stale release timing creates conflict, editable wiki pages flatten or falsify people, and hour-three intimacy can become parasocial sunk cost. A better product must preserve complete recordings while enabling immediate topic entry, easy exit, exact context, corrections, participant control and work-centered identity. Saelee Oh's art and Critter Fleming's Momofuku work stay visible beside the dating material. All five fuzzy Saelee suggestions are rejected as unusable untimestamped fragments; the canonical name is repaired explicitly. The final pilcrow glyph is nonlexical, and damaged song/reprise words are not invented. Named turns remain withheld pending held-out acoustic validation.

source_notes.claim: Asian Americans were less than four or five percent of the United States.
source_notes.assessment: The 2010 Census counted 4.8% Asian alone and 5.6% Asian alone or in combination. The in-room 5.6% correction is valid only with that definition.

source_notes.claim: Affirmative action at UCLA worked against Asian applicants.
source_notes.assessment: Race could not be considered in UC admissions after California Proposition 209 took effect. The episode's simple causal explanation for enrollment/admission outcomes is therefore inaccurate.

source_notes.claim: Vomiting and chewing/spitting were ordinary ways to become temporarily irresistible.
source_notes.assessment: These are disordered-eating behaviors, not safe weight-control methods. The archive documents the admission without endorsing it or diagnosing a specific disorder.

source_notes.claim: Stopping daily cannabis is either harmless or necessarily caused a particular symptom.
source_notes.assessment: Cannabis withdrawal can include irritability, nervousness, sleep problems, appetite change and other symptoms, but the episode does not establish which, if any, Saelee experienced.

source_notes.claim: Aggressive oral sex itself caused the nosebleed.
source_notes.assessment: The participant and room reject that simple causal joke. Sinus irritation and intranasal cocaine are recognized nosebleed causes; the exact cause here cannot be diagnosed from the recording.

source_notes.claim: Snorted cocaine has no relevant nasal health context.
source_notes.assessment: Repeated snorting can lead to nosebleeds and nasal damage, among other risks.

source_notes.claim: Continuing an act after wanting it to end is required by politeness.
source_notes.assessment: Consent can be withdrawn at any point. Intoxication and social pressure complicate action but do not remove the right to stop.

speaker_policy: Public cast and Saelee Oh may be identified at episode level where introduced. The three dates, referring agent, private partners, spouses, young roadie, fan tailor, venue workers, family members, account owners, sexual partners, residences, routes, phone numbers, private messages and explicit images remain excluded from discovery. Overlap, song lyrics, seating, physical contact, cake throw, wedding video, phone-message reading and the damaged tail require acoustic/video validation. No line-level named dialogue publishes until held-out voice validation passes.
